en-US.author: General Action, Inc.
en-US.description: Open-source agentic development environment for running coding agents in parallel.
en-US.longDescription:
Emdash is an open-source agentic development environment for running coding agents in parallel across isolated Git worktrees.

What you can do:
- Run multiple coding agents at once without juggling terminals.
- Keep every agent isolated in its own Git worktree and branch.
- Send issues and tickets from Linear, GitHub, Jira, GitLab, Asana, Featurebase, Monday.com, Forgejo, Plain, or YouTrack into an agent.
- Review diffs, create pull requests, inspect CI checks, and merge from one place.
- Work locally or on your own remote machines over SSH/SFTP.
- Schedule recurring agent runs and preview apps in a built-in browser.
en-US.name: Emdash
en-US.releaseNotes:
This release improves Git authentication, Windows compatibility, and SSH responsiveness. It also reduces background fetch overhead, fixes pane shortcuts after switching tasks, and adds an in-app signup for Emdash 2.0 early access.
Highlights
- The project's Git credentials setting now applies to Emdash's own local Git operations, including push, pull, and fetch. Choosing System uses the machine's credentials, while an account explicitly selected for an operation still takes precedence.
- Join the Emdash 2.0 waitlist directly from the sidebar, with your email and an optional note about your team or workflow. The card can be dismissed for the current release.
Fixes
- Commit & Push and other Git network operations on Windows authenticate correctly through the connected account, fixing failures where pushing from a terminal worked but pushing from Emdash did not.
- Agent hooks on Windows run correctly when launched through Git Bash, including Claude Code hooks. Prompt and assistant text passed to hooks is no longer misinterpreted as shell commands.
- Windows builds resolve the bundled SSH dependency correctly, fixing a module-loading error reported in v1.2.10.
- SSH connections send handshake and interactive traffic without waiting for TCP buffering, improving responsiveness when connecting to and working on remote machines.
- Background Git fetches wait after the previous fetch finishes and back off when a repository is slow. Fetches also avoid unnecessary metadata writes and automatic maintenance, reducing disk work and contention with other Git operations.
- Self-hosted Git integrations correctly match remotes that use custom HTTP or HTTPS ports, including Forgejo instances.
- Pane shortcuts remain active after switching tasks or projects when a terminal or input has already received focus.

zh-CN.description: 可并行运行编码智能体的开源智能体开发环境。
zh-CN.longDescription:
Emdash 是一个开源的智能体开发环境，可在隔离的 Git worktree 中并行运行编码智能体。

你可以：
- 同时运行多个编码智能体，无需在终端之间手忙脚乱。
- 让每个智能体隔离在自己的 Git worktree 和分支中。
- 将 Linear、GitHub、Jira、GitLab、Asana、Featurebase、Monday.com、Forgejo、Plain 或 YouTrack 的问题和工单发送给智能体。
- 在同一个地方审查 diff、创建 PR、检查 CI 并合并。
- 在本地或通过 SSH/SFTP 在你自己的远程机器上工作。
- 定时循环运行智能体，并在内置浏览器中预览应用。
